losers.hypothesis: Extract build loop into a sync per-chunk scanChunk kernel with ScanState marshaling; sync iteration for array inputs.

failure_analysis.what: Score 0.897 vs 0.898 baseline: no measurable change (runs 0.897/0.892/0.905, within ~4% spread). Executor labelled it a regression.
failure_analysis.why: Moving the loop into a sync function did not change the per-byte work. The executor cited a 0.946 baseline and a ~10% slowdown from state marshaling; that does not match the sealed benchmark (0.898) and with ~16 chunks per build marshaling cost is negligible. Likely cause: the inner loop shape is unchanged, so the async/sync split alone yields nothing.
failure_analysis.lesson: The sync-kernel refactor alone is neutral. Gains must come from the inner loop (tight string-skip loop, fast reject), which is where 75% of bytes sit. Keep state in locals; do not restructure around a state object.
